What the Present Must Keep: the Weight Between, the Speed of the Record, and the Wall It Survives

Jeromie Beasley

2 November 2026 (version 1.1)

AI-assisted. The ideas and research direction are the author’s; AI tools (Claude, Anthropic) were used for literature search, computation, drafting and typesetting. All simulations are runs of S. McCormick’s public code and of finite models on a cloud computer, not laboratory experiments.

Abstract

A reduced description must carry, besides what it reads now, whatever the future still needs: that difference is memory. We put four finite results and one physical system in a single line. (i) In finite dimensions the first dimV\dim V readings decide every future reading, and a present reading needs no memory exactly when it closes under the evolution; under reduction the memory is the kernel BeDuCBe^{Du}C and its zero-lag trace is the coupling energy EB=∥PH(1−P)∥F2E_B=\lVert PH(1-P)\rVert_F^2, which is also the speed of the kept sector and the variance of its energy. (ii) Read at powers of the gap, the same weight is the projector metric (k=−2k=-2), the static optical response (k=−1k=-1), the energy variance (k=0k=0) and the oscillator-strength budget (k=+1k=+1); log-convexity of these moments, a classical fact, makes the known bound α0≤2(g2F)1/3\alpha_0\le2(g^2F)^{1/3} a single ladder step, with equality when one gap value carries all the coupling. (iii) The log-odds τ=logdet(I−C)−logdetC\tau=\log\det(I-C)-\log\det C of a cut obeys τ̇2≤4gS\dot\tau^2\le4gS with S=Tr[(C(I−C))−1]S=\operatorname{Tr}[(C(I-C))^{-1}], so a record moves no faster than 2EBS2\sqrt{E_BS}. (iv) The projector is blind to an added constant; a clock reads only differences of constants; the operator’s contour ledger reads the constant itself. (v) For idempotents the tangent form has neutral signature and can change sign. In an explicit chart the wall sits exactly on the line where the projector becomes orthogonal, the null direction there is a nilpotent push, and the contour ledger passes through unchanged in kind. A source inserted into the ledger rebuilds the wall when it is read in full; the geometry built from its real part alone is blind to the wall and keeps one trace of it, being positive semidefinite exactly on the wall. The physical case is neutrinos leaving a collapsing patch of the early universe. Their kept population obeys the one-mode form of the speed limit, which free streaming nearly saturates. Pre-registered runs of McCormick’s code show that the history of decoupling, not only its end, sets the threshold for black-hole formation. A first-principles ledger built from the light that has already left carries about half of that memory; the rest sits in angular moments that no fluid closure keeps. Every claim is graded.

Grades.

[T]: written proof here (Appendix A). [C]: cited result, restated. [N]: computation reported with its script. [M]: measured in a simulation run, with pre-registered kill lines. [H]: interpretation. [L]: finite statement checked in Lean at a named repository.

The question

Every description that keeps less than everything faces two questions. What must the present keep in order to predict every reading the future can still make? And what does it cost to move what is kept? This paper answers both in finite dimensions, joins the answers to a single quantity, the weight between a kept sector and the rest, and then tests the result on one physical system where the answer matters: neutrinos that stop scattering while a region of the early universe collapses.

The pieces were developed separately: the memory and weight results in The Weight Between [1], the record’s speed limit in The Offset Speed Limit [2], the transition-resolved optics in Light Keeps the Ledger [3], the sign wall in The Ledger Outlives the Metric [4], and the neutrino runs in When the Neutrinos Leave [5]. Here they are made one argument, every imported result is restated with its proof, and four links between them are new: the identification of the open fourth rung of the gap ladder (Section 3.1); the neutrino speed bound as the one-mode speed limit (Section 4); the second reader of a constant (Section 5); and the location and anatomy of the sign wall together with what a source can read there (Section 6).

Memory is what a reduction leaves out

Let VV be finite-dimensional, L:V→VL:V\to V the evolution and R:V→WR:V\to W the present reading. Write N∞=⋂n≥0kerRLnN_\infty=\bigcap_{n\ge0}\ker RL^n for the differences that are never seen and Vpred=V/N∞V_{\mathrm pred}=V/N_\infty.

Theorem 1 (the future is decided early). RLnv=RLnwRL^nv=RL^nw for all nn if and only if it holds for n<dimVn<\dim V. N∞N_\infty is LL-invariant and lies in kerR\ker R. [T; L [1]]

Theorem 2 (least predictor). If a linear FF determines every future reading, then kerF⊆N∞\ker F\subseteq N_\infty and rankF≥dimVpred\operatorname{rank}F\ge\dim V_{\mathrm pred}; VpredV_{\mathrm pred} with its induced dynamics is a predictor of least dimension. [T; L]

Theorem 3 (when the present closes). The present reading needs no memory (Rv=0⇒RLv=0Rv=0\Rightarrow RLv=0) if and only if RL=ARRL=AR for some linear AA; then N∞=kerRN_\infty=\ker R. Otherwise the present must carry dimVpred−rankR>0\dim V_{\mathrm pred}-\operatorname{rank}R>0 further numbers. [T; L]

Theorem 1 is the finite observability statement of control theory [10]; its use here is as the definition of memory: memory is the gap in Theorem 3.

This holds for every idempotent, orthogonal or not. For orthogonal PP moving under Ṗ=−i[H,P]\dot P=-i[H,P], g:=12∥Ṗ∥F2=12∥[H,P]∥F2=EB,and g=VarψH when P=|ψ⟩⟨ψ|,(3)g:=\tfrac12\lVert \dot P\rVert_F^2=\tfrac12\lVert [H,P]\rVert_F^2=E_B,\qquad\text{and }g=\operatorname{Var}_\psi H\text{ when }P=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi| ,\qquad(3) so one number is at once the speed of the kept sector, the zero-lag memory (2) and, for a pure state, the energy variance (Anandan–Aharonov [12]) [T; N: worst relative difference 4×10−154\times 10^{-15} over 300 cases [1]]. The record and its speed limit

Cut an orthogonal projector PP on ℂn\mathbb C^n by a fixed isometry E:ℂm→ℂnE:\mathbb C^m\to\mathbb C^n into the accessible block C=E†PEC=E^\dagger PE, with 0<C<I0<C<I. Then C−C2=P12P12†C-C^2=P_{12}P_{12}^\dagger [T; L [3]], the census of the cut. The offset τ=Tr[log(I−C)−logC]=logdet(I−C)−logdetC(4)\tau=\operatorname{Tr}[\log(I-C)-\log C]=\log\det(I-C)-\log\det C\qquad(4) is the log-odds of the block being empty against full [7]. The census loses its sign: C=diag(0.2,0.8)C=\operatorname{diag}(0.2,0.8) and diag(0.2,0.2)\operatorname{diag}(0.2,0.2) have the same census and offsets 00 and log16\log16.

Theorem 8 (the offset speed limit). For a differentiable family of orthogonal projectors, with g=12∥Ṗ∥F2g=\tfrac12\lVert \dot P\rVert_F^2 and S=Tr[(C(I−C))−1]S=\operatorname{Tr}[(C(I-C))^{-1}], τ̇2≤4gS.(5)\dot\tau^2\le4gS .\qquad(5) Equality holds if and only if Ṗ=λ[P,[P,F]]\dot P=\lambda[P,[P,F]] for real λ\lambda, where F=EWE†F=EWE^\dagger, W=−(C(I−C))−1W=-(C(I-C))^{-1}. [T; for rank one a bound of Mandelstam–Tamm type [13]; N: largest ratio 0.9110.911 over 500 driven cases, equality case to 7×10−97\times 10^{-9} [2]]

One accessible mode.

For m=1m=1 and a pure state, C=AC=A is the population kept in the accessible mode, τ=log[(1−A)/A]\tau=\log[(1-A)/A], τ̇=−Ȧ/(A(1−A))\dot\tau=-\dot A/(A(1-A)), S=1/(A(1−A))S=1/(A(1-A)), and (5) becomes Ȧ2≤4gA(1−A),g=VarψH.(6)\dot A^2\le4\,g\,A(1-A),\qquad g=\operatorname{Var}_\psi H .\qquad(6) Under unitary evolution VarψH\operatorname{Var}_\psi H is conserved, so gg is its value at the start [T]. For an orthogonal rank-one projector path in ℂ2\mathbb C^2 the gap is exact: 4gS−τ̇2=4(Imb‾ḃ)2/(c(1−c))24gS-\dot\tau^2=4(\operatorname{Im}\bar b\dot b)^2/(c(1-c))^2 for P=(cbb‾1−c)P=\begin{pmatrix}c&b\\\bar b&1-c\end{pmatrix} [T; L; N [2]]. Equation (6) is exactly the speed bound found for neutrinos in [5]; Section 7 uses it.

Two readers of a constant

Proposition 10 (what sees sH+cIsH+cI). Let s>0s>0 and c∈ℝc\in\mathbb R. (a) The spectral projectors of HH, and the tensor QQ of Section 3, are unchanged by H↦sH+cIH\mapsto sH+cI. (b) Every expectation value in a single branch is unchanged by H↦H+cIH\mapsto H+cI; two branches with constants c1,c2c_1,c_2 acquire the relative phase −(c1−c2)t-(c_1-c_2)t. (c) For a positive operator KK and a contour Γ\Gamma enclosing a selected cluster of kk eigenvalues λj\lambda_j and kept away from the negative axis, the contour ledger ZΓ(K)=12πi∮ΓlogzTr(z−K)−1dzZ_\Gamma(K)=\frac1{2\pi i}\oint_\Gamma\log z\,\operatorname{Tr}(z-K)^{-1}dz obeys, for α>0\alpha>0 and every cc with λj+c>0\lambda_j+c>0 and the shifted contour still separating the cluster, ZΓ+c(K+cI)=ZΓ(K)+∑jlog(1+c/λj),ZαΓ(αK)=ZΓ(K)+klogα,(7)Z_{\Gamma+c}(K+cI)=Z_\Gamma(K)+\sum_j\log(1+c/\lambda_j),\qquad Z_{\alpha\Gamma}(\alpha K)=Z_\Gamma(K)+k\log\alpha ,\qquad(7) while the projector does not move. [T; L for (a) and (b) [2]; (c) C [4, Prop. 30]; N: (c) to every printed digit, projector change <10−15<10^{-15}; L for the eigenvalue identity in (c)]

So the geometry of the kept subspace sees neither seconds nor a constant. Among readings of a state, only a comparison of two clocks sees a constant, and then only as a difference: this is how gravity first appeared in a neutron interferometer [19] and how satellite clocks are corrected. The operator’s own contour ledger reads the constant directly. The ledger and the clock are therefore the two readers of a weight, and the projector is the reader of a direction [H]. The proposal of [2] that a pair of clocks of different kinds can test whether every form of energy carries the same weight (a strontium optical clock against a thorium-229 nuclear clock, whose ratio cancels the universal part exactly) is the experimental form of reading (b) [N: one year of the ratio resolves a coupling to 7.6×10−117.6\times 10^{-11} in a model with stated inputs; H].

The wall the record survives

Two kinds of wall

For an orthogonal projector the tangent pairing is a Gram form, Q(V,V)=∥(1−P)VP∥F2≥0Q(V,V)=\lVert (1-P)VP\rVert_F^2\ge0: the metric can lose rank but never sign [3]. For an idempotent that is not orthogonal it can do both.

Theorem 11 (neutral signature). On the full real tangent space of rank-kk idempotents in Mn(ℂ)M_n(\mathbb C), q(D)=12ReTrD2q(D)=\tfrac12\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}D^2 is nondegenerate with signature (2k(n−k),2k(n−k))(2k(n-k),2k(n-k)). [T; L for the coordinate algebra [4]; N: confirmed for five (n,k)(n,k) from the null space of D↦PD+DP−DD\mapsto PD+DP-D; the Hermitian slice is positive definite]

Theorem 12 (a negative direction lifts the overlap above the cap). For a C2C^2 family of rank-kk idempotents with D=P′(0)D=P'(0), ReTr(P(0)P(t))=k−12ReTr(D2)t2+o(t2)\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}(P(0)P(t))=k-\tfrac12\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}(D^2)\,t^2+o(t^2). If q(D)<0q(D)<0 the overlap exceeds kk for all small t≠0t\ne0. [T; L [4]; N: 40-digit check, relative error 3.5×10−63.5\times 10^{-6}]

For orthogonal projectors Tr(PR)≤k\operatorname{Tr}(PR)\le k always; the cap is a property of the orthogonal class, and losing it is what a sign wall means.

An explicit wall, and where it sits

On |x|,|y|<14|x|,|y|<\tfrac14 put z=x+iyz=x+iy, w=x+iy2w=x+iy^2 and P(x,y)=11+zw(1wzzw),H=(2+y10)P+(5+y5)(I−P).(8)P(x,y)=\frac1{1+zw}\begin{pmatrix}1&w\\z&zw\end{pmatrix},\qquad H=(2+\tfrac y{10})P+(5+\tfrac y5)(I-P).\qquad(8)

Theorem 13 (a wall without an exceptional point). P2=PP^2=P, TrP=1\operatorname{Tr}P=1, and on x=0x=0 the form gij=12ReTr(∂iP∂jP)g_{ij}=\tfrac12\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}(\partial_iP\,\partial_jP) is (1−y3)−2diag(1,−2y)(1-y^3)^{-2}\operatorname{diag}(1,-2y): positive definite for y<0y<0, indefinite for y>0y>0. The eigenvalues of HH stay separated by 3+y/103+y/10; the circle |z−2|=0.4|z-2|=0.4 encloses one of them, giving count N=1N=1 and ledger Z=log(2+y/10)Z=\log(2+y/10), regular and varying through the wall. [C [4]; T (A.8); N: exact symbolic check and contour quadrature to 3×10−163\times 10^{-16}]

The new statement is where the wall is and what its null direction is.

Proposition 14 (the wall is the edge of the self-adjoint slice). In the box of (8): (i) P(x,y)P(x,y) is self-adjoint if and only if y=0y=0. (ii) On y=0y=0, g=(1+x2)−2diag(1,0)g=(1+x^2)^{-2}\operatorname{diag}(1,0), so detg=0\det g=0 along the whole line, and detg\det g changes sign across it. (iii) ∂zP\partial_zP is nilpotent everywhere; on y=0y=0, ∂yP=i∂zP\partial_yP=i\,\partial_zP is a nonzero, non-self-adjoint nilpotent, so 12ReTr(∂yP)2=0\tfrac12\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Tr}(\partial_yP)^2=0 while 12∥∂yP∥F2>0\tfrac12\lVert \partial_yP\rVert_F^2>0. [T (A.8); L for (i) and the nilpotent square in (iii); N: symbolic check, and on a 401×401401\times 401 grid the zero set of detg\det g is y=0y=0 for every xx]

So the metric goes null exactly where the projector is most ordinary, and the direction it cannot price is a push off the orthogonal projectors that squares to zero. The example after Theorem 2 of [4], a self-adjoint point carrying a negative tangent, and the wall of Theorem 13 are one phenomenon. Part (iii) also shows that the weight 12∥Ṗ∥F2\tfrac12\lVert \dot P\rVert_F^2 of Section 3 stays positive through the wall: it cannot see it. Whether the wall sits on the self-adjoint locus in every analytic chart is untested.

What a source can read

The bare ledger ZZ cannot see the projector at all: with H=λP+μ(1−P)H=\lambda P+\mu(1-P), Z=klogλZ=k\log\lambda depends only on λ\lambda, while gg depends only on PP [T [4]]. A probe restores the link.

Theorem 15 (source insertion). For invertible KK, a contour Γ\Gamma separating a cluster with an analytic logarithm, and a fixed BB, ddtZΓ(K+tB)|0=Tr(PΓK−1B),(9)\frac{d}{dt}Z_\Gamma(K+tB)\Big|_0=\operatorname{Tr}(P_\Gamma K^{-1}B),\qquad(9) including clusters with Jordan blocks. Write q(b)q(b) for (9) with the probe B=bb†B=bb^\dagger. For any such KK the complex readings at eie_i, ei+eje_i+e_j, ei+ieje_i+ie_j recover PΓK−1P_\Gamma K^{-1} by polarisation. If K=K†>0K=K^\dagger>0, then q(b)=b†PΓK−1b=∑λ∈Γλ−1∥Pλb∥2≥0q(b)=b^\dagger P_\Gamma K^{-1}b=\sum_{\lambda\in\Gamma}\lambda^{-1}\lVert P_\lambda b\rVert^2\ge0, its null space is kerPΓ\ker P_\Gamma, and the recovered PΓK−1P_\Gamma K^{-1} has support PΓP_\Gamma. [T; C [4, 3]; N: finite differences of ZZ against (9), worst relative error 7×10−107\times 10^{-10} with Jordan clusters; tomography from measured derivatives to 6×10−116\times 10^{-11}]

For an oblique projector the response need not be positive: with K=(2905)K=\begin{pmatrix}2&9\\0&5\end{pmatrix}, PΓ=(1−300)P_\Gamma=\begin{pmatrix}1&-3\\0&0\end{pmatrix} and b=(1,1)b=(1,1), q(b)=−1q(b)=-1 although both eigenvalues are positive [T [4]; N]. Light’s probe-span result [3, Sec. 4.9b] already states that full response needs probes resolving the imaginary cross components. At the wall this becomes sharp.

Proposition 16 (full and real-only readout at the wall). For the chart (8), with every q(b)q(b) measured as a finite difference of the contour ledger: (a) the full readout, polarising with complex probes, rebuilds PP to 9×10−109\times10^{-10} and the metric to 8×10−68\times10^{-6}, and places the wall at y=−3.8×10−7y=-3.8\times10^{-7}; (b) the real-only readout, Req\operatorname{Re}q, recovers only the self-adjoint part of PΓK−1P_\Gamma K^{-1}; the geometry built from it is positive definite throughout, smallest eigenvalue 0.0930.093 on a 41×4141\times41 grid over |x|,|y|≤0.24|x|,|y|\le0.24; (c) the smallest eigenvalue of 12(P+P†)/λ\tfrac12(P+P^\dagger)/\lambda is negative everywhere off y=0y=0 (down to −0.011-0.011) and exactly zero on all 41 grid points of y=0y=0; (d) for an orthogonal-projector family the real-only readout equals the full readout to 1.3×10−111.3\times10^{-11} and there is no wall. [N: kill lines written before the run, all met]

The metric a source rebuilds therefore shows the sign wall when the source is read with its phase, and does not when only its real part is read. Part (b) is generic: the self-adjoint parts of independent tangents always give a positive form, so the real readout cannot locate the wall. It keeps one trace of it, part (c): its own response is positive semidefinite exactly on the wall and indefinite everywhere else in the box [N; H].

The physical case: neutrinos leaving a collapsing patch

Primordial black holes heavier than about 106M⊙10^6M_\odot form while neutrinos, 41% of the radiation, stop scattering. McCormick evolved them with their angle-resolved transport equation in spherical general relativity and found that free streaming raises the collapse threshold, by ΔCl,c/Cl,c≃0.235Rν\Delta C_{l,c}/C_{l,c}\simeq0.235R_\nu; under gradual decoupling, κ=H(ϵdec/ϵ)3\kappa=H(\epsilon_{\mathrm dec}/\epsilon)^3, only a share G=(δc−δcfluid)/(δcinst−δcfluid)G=(\delta_c-\delta_c^{\mathrm fluid})/(\delta_c^{\mathrm inst}-\delta_c^{\mathrm fluid}) survives [8]. Here ϵ=1/(aHrm)\epsilon=1/(aHr_m); in his initial data the conformal time in units of rmr_m equals ϵ\epsilon, so ϵ\epsilon is the time variable below [T].

The cut and the weight

One Fourier mode of the linearised intensity evolves under ∂ϵv=−(ikM+σ(ϵ)(I−P0))v\partial_\epsilon v=-(ikM+\sigma(\epsilon)(I-P_0))v in the normalised Legendre basis, with MM real symmetric tridiagonal, Mℓ,ℓ+1=Mℓ+1,ℓ=cℓ=(ℓ+1)/(2ℓ+1)(2ℓ+3)M_{\ell,\ell+1}=M_{\ell+1,\ell}=c_\ell=(\ell+1)/\sqrt{(2\ell+1)(2\ell+3)}, P0=|0⟩⟨0|P_0=|0\rangle\langle0| and σ=ϵdecn/ϵn+1\sigma=\epsilon_{\mathrm dec}^n/\epsilon^{n+1}. Collisions conserve the isotropic part and remove the rest. The kept sector is |0⟩|0\rangle, the density, and the weight between it and everything that streams is EB=∥P0kM(1−P0)∥F2=k2c02=k2/3,(10)E_B=\lVert P_0\,kM\,(1-P_0)\rVert_F^2=k^2c_0^2=k^2/3,\qquad(10) so EB=k/3\sqrt{E_B}=k/\sqrt3 is the radiation sound speed [T]. All non-normality of the single-rate operator lies on the density–flux link, 18∥[L,L*]∥F2=κ2k2/3\tfrac18\lVert [L,L^\ast]\rVert_F^2=\kappa^2k^2/3 [T [5, 6]]. Collisions act on the hidden moments only, so the kept population changes only through that link: light writes the kept sector’s record and collisions only erase what is hidden [T].

The memory kernel.

In the relaxation model every hidden moment is damped at the same rate, so the hidden propagator is exact, UQ(t,r)=e−[Σ(t)−Σ(r)]e−ik(t−r)MQQU_Q(t,r)=e^{-[\Sigma(t)-\Sigma(r)]}e^{-ik(t-r)M_{QQ}} with Σ=−ϵdecn/(nϵn)\Sigma=-\epsilon_{\mathrm dec}^n/(n\epsilon^n), and eliminating the hidden block gives ȧ(t)=S(t)−k2c02∫st[UQ(t,r)]11a(r)dr,(11)\dot a(t)=S(t)-k^2c_0^2\int_s^t[U_Q(t,r)]_{11}\,a(r)\,dr ,\qquad(11) which is (1) with B=kc0⟨1|B=kc_0\langle1|, collisions entering as a time-dependent damping of the hidden block [T].

The speed limit.

With A=|a0|2A=|a_0|^2, the one-mode limit (6) with g=EBg=E_B is Ȧ2≤4EBA(1−A),(12)\dot A^2\le4E_B\,A(1-A),\qquad(12) proved directly in [5] with collisions included, since they only shorten the state [T; L [5]]. For pure streaming it is Corollary 9 with Var|0⟩(kM)=k2/3\operatorname{Var}_{|0\rangle}(kM)=k^2/3 conserved (drift 2×10−142\times10^{-14}), and the bound is met almost exactly: largest ratio 0.999960.99996 [N]. Gradual decoupling holds the record back (Figure 3).

A population that decouples more abruptly by the same nominal time keeps less of its effect: a history-blind rule, which would give the interpolated n=3n=3 value, misses Test D by 0.1460.146 against a kill line of 0.080.08. Test B is unchanged by a tenfold higher rate cap (−0.00003-0.00003) and by a finer grid (+0.00008+0.00008). A broad profile that collapses twice as late keeps the same share or less (G=0.181G=0.181, 0.0450.045 against 0.1900.190, 0.0630.063), so the collapse time alone does not set the clock [M]. A memory form built on the kept sector, with one weight fitted to McCormick’s curve and frozen, predicted Tests C, B, D as 0.6630.663, 0.2460.246, 0.1180.118 before they were run, all inside the kill line [M; fit].

Where the memory sits

Two neutrino states with the same density, flux and anisotropic stress, differing only in the ℓ=3\ell=3 or ℓ=4\ell=4 moment, were evolved under the same history with the difference planted at time ϵs\epsilon_s. Planted at or after decoupling, the difference returns into density, flux and stress at the level of 2–13% (8–10% read at ϵ=4\epsilon=4); planted deep in the coupled era it is erased by exp[−ϵdecn/(nϵsn)]\exp[-\epsilon_{\mathrm dec}^n/(n\epsilon_s^n)], down to 10−3010^{-30}. Every on/off call was written before the run and all came out as predicted; solving (11) from the closed-form UQU_Q alone reproduces the full system to between 5×10−85\times10^{-8} and 7×10−77\times10^{-7} [N [5]]. In the language of Theorem 3: density, flux and stress do not close under the decoupling evolution, and the angular moments a fluid closure drops are among the numbers the present must carry.

How much of the memory is in the ledger

The last test asks the question of Section 4 directly: is the record written by light into the kept sector the whole memory? The kinetic model fixes the ledger with nothing fitted: S(ϵ)=∑kwk|a0(k,ϵ)|2S(\epsilon)=\sum_kw_k|a_0(k,\epsilon)|^2 with the profile weights wk∝k2e−k2/2w_k\propto k^2e^{-k^2/2}, and the entry written at time ϵ\epsilon is L(ϵ)=−dS/dϵL(\epsilon)=-dS/d\epsilon. If the threshold reads the ledger linearly, Δδc=∫W(ϵ)L(ϵ)dϵ\Delta\delta_c=\int W(\epsilon)L(\epsilon)\,d\epsilon with a listening weight WW, then G=∫WLhist∫WLinst(13)G=\frac{\int W\,L_{\mathrm hist}}{\int W\,L_{\mathrm inst}}\qquad(13) with no free parameter once WW is measured. WW was measured by short bursts of free streaming, κ=0\kappa=0 on [ϵb,1.25ϵb][\epsilon_b,1.25\epsilon_b], inside a fully coupled history, eight burst times, full threshold searches. Five kill lines were written before the runs [M]:

line test outcome
K1 two bursts add pass: 0.001333=0.000889+0.0004440.001333=0.000889+0.000444
K2 nine predicted GG within 0.050.05 fail: worst miss 0.1010.101 (Test C)
K3 a coupling burst has the opposite sign pass: −0.00904-0.00904, −0.00194-0.00194

The listening weight falls from 0.0280.028 per ledger entry at ϵb=0.25\epsilon_b=0.25 to zero by ϵb=6\epsilon_b=6 (Figure 4). The shape of GG is right late and too low early, and the size is about half: the ledger reading of the instantaneous shift is 0.01570.0157 against the measured 0.03060.0306, short by a factor 1.91.9–2.32.3 for every history. Measuring WW the opposite way, from coupling bursts on a free-streaming base, fails worse [M].

The reading is Theorem 3 measured. The kept population is a present reading that does not close: late collisions stop neutrinos that are already in the hidden moments, on their way out, and hand their momentum back to the plasma. That moves the threshold strongly while barely changing the ledger. So the record of when the neutrinos left is written by light, and the ledger of light that has left holds about half of it; the other half is carried by light still in transit, in exactly the moments Section 7.3 found holding the memory [M; H]. A ledger that also books the hidden-moment flux is the natural next object; it is untested.

Limits and open steps

  • The finite theorems stand on their stated hypotheses. The identifications of the rungs with memory, light, time and budget are readings of standard quantities [H]; Proposition 5 is classical.

  • Proposition 14 is proved for one chart. Whether a sign wall of an analytic idempotent family always sits on its self-adjoint locus is untested.

  • Nothing here derives a gravitational field equation, an area law or a spacetime metric. The sign wall is a wall of a parameter form, not a horizon [4].

  • The neutrino runs use McCormick’s relaxation-time collision term, spherical symmetry and a Gaussian profile. The ledger test used a fully coupled base at κ/H=104\kappa/H=10^4, not the cap, and its coupling bursts were ramped over ten steps because a direct switch crashes the code. K5 rests on one approximately matched pair.

  • The Lean coverage is finite and named per statement; analytic, contour and variational steps are written proofs.

Summary

The present must keep whatever its reading does not close over, and the cost of moving what it keeps is one number, the weight between. That number, read at four powers of the gap, is memory geometry, light’s response, the energy variance and the oscillator budget, tied by one convexity. A record written across a cut moves no faster than twice the square root of the weight times the cut’s sensitivity. The kept subspace sees neither a scale nor a constant; a clock sees constants as differences; the contour ledger sees them directly. When the tangent form changes sign, the ledger passes through, the wall sits where the projector becomes orthogonal, and a probe sees it only when read with its phase. Neutrinos leaving a collapsing patch obey the same speed limit, remember how they left, and keep half of that memory in the light that has gone and half in the light still going.

With |x|,|y|<14|x|,|y|<\tfrac14, 𝒜≥1−2|y|3−2x2|y|5>0.96\mathcal A\ge1-2|y|^3-2x^2|y|^5>0.96 and ℬ≥2−4|y|3−3x2|y|3−x2|y|>1.9\mathcal B\ge2-4|y|^3-3x^2|y|^3-x^2|y|>1.9, so detg\det g has the sign of −y-y for every xx: positive below the line, negative above. ▫\square

A.9 Theorem 15.

With R(z)=(z−K)−1R(z)=(z-K)^{-1} and ddtR=RBR\frac d{dt}R=RBR, ∂tZ=12πi∮logzTr(RBR)dz=−12πi∮logz∂zTr(BR)dz\partial_tZ=\frac1{2\pi i}\oint\log z\,\operatorname{Tr}(RBR)\,dz=-\frac1{2\pi i}\oint\log z\,\partial_z\operatorname{Tr}(BR)\,dz. Integrating by parts on the closed contour gives 12πi∮z−1Tr(BR)dz=Tr(BPΓK−1)\frac1{2\pi i}\oint z^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}(BR)\,dz=\operatorname{Tr}(BP_\Gamma K^{-1}) by functional calculus, z−1z^{-1} being analytic inside Γ\Gamma. For K=K†>0K=K^\dagger>0, PΓK−1=∑λ∈Γλ−1Pλ≥0P_\Gamma K^{-1}=\sum_{\lambda\in\Gamma}\lambda^{-1}P_\lambda\ge0 with range RanPΓ\operatorname{Ran}P_\Gamma. Polarisation: q(ei+ej)−q(ei)−q(ej)=2ReAijq(e_i+e_j)-q(e_i)-q(e_j)=2\operatorname{Re}A_{ij} and q(ei+iej)−q(ei)−q(ej)=−2ImAijq(e_i+ie_j)-q(e_i)-q(e_j)=-2\operatorname{Im}A_{ij} for Hermitian AA; for general AA the complex readings give Aij+AjiA_{ij}+A_{ji} and Aij−AjiA_{ij}-A_{ji} separately, while their real parts give only 12(A+A†)\tfrac12(A+A^\dagger), which is Proposition 16(b). ▫\square
